productBase.note: The AttemptId product fix eabc8b88 is the base; this block changes tests only.

whatWasWrongBefore: The consumer raised a tokenless OperationCanceledException after a wall clock delay, which JobConsumerMessageFilter treats as a reported consumer fault rather than a lost worker.
Sent.Any<GetJobAttemptStatus>() and Consumed.Any<GetJobAttemptStatus>() discarded their boolean result and asserted nothing.
Fixed delays and large Quartz jumps were timing hope instead of controlled causality.
A terminal JobFaulted alone does not distinguish the claimed suspect path from the direct reported fault path.
The fixture was marked Flaky and its sibling tests were assertion poor.
mechanism: The same test local receive suppression as the retry sibling. The one reported JobAttemptFaulted of the started attempt is suppressed on both job and job-attempt, so the job service has to judge the worker through its own status checks.
provenChain: started attempt recorded by the consumer
exactly two suppressions of the same MessageId at endpoints job and job-attempt
at least two job status checks delivered to the instance
a suspect fault of the same AttemptId, with a different MessageId, carrying no RetryDelay
exactly one terminal JobFaulted for this job
additionalNegatives: no redelivery or consumer retry of the suppressed message

assertions: suppressed.AttemptId == StartedAttemptId (the attempt the worker actually started)

the consumer job duration, which is simulated work and not test synchronisation

The filter made the probe non discriminating; it was repeated over the whole fixture and is red there.
correctedOwnProbe.consequence: Every sabotage result reported here comes from a whole fixture run.
